blocks.content: A river system consists of the main river and its tributaries. The area drained by a river and its tributaries is called a drainage basin. The boundary separating two drainage basins is known as a watershed.
The boundary separating two drainage basins is known as a watershed.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: A river system is composed of the primary river together with all its tributaries.
A drainage basin encompasses the entire geographical area drained by a river and its tributaries.
A watershed acts as the elevated physical boundary dividing two adjacent river basins.
Crucial hydrological elements include the Source (origin), Tributary (joining stream), Confluence (meeting point), and Watershed (highland divider).

blocks.content: • Tributary – smaller stream joining main river.

items: Direct definitions of 'Watershed' versus 'Drainage Basin' are frequently tested in geography preliminary exams.
Remember that a 'Confluence' specifically refers to the meeting point of two rivers.
Distinguish clearly between a tributary (stream joining a main river) and the river's source (its origin).

blocks.content: • Confluence – meeting point of two rivers.
• Watershed – highland dividing two river basins.
